_comment: Per-chart narratives. CI (build_prompt.py -> GitHub Models -> write_narrative.py) overwrites these from live numbers; this committed copy is the fallback so the page always reads well. source = 'fallback' | 'github-models'.

notes.basket: The breakfast basket, an average of global prices for coffee, sugar, wheat, and orange juice indexed to 2015=100, currently stands at 132, reflecting approximately a 32% increase since 2015. This headline climb is primarily recent and uneven across the commodities measured. The basket consolidates price movements of key soft commodities relevant to breakfast consumption. It highlights notable overall inflation in this segment but does not imply uniform rises across all included items.
notes.movers: Coffee has exhibited the largest increase, up 93% since 2015, followed by orange juice at 22%, wheat at 7%, and sugar at 5%. These changes are largely driven by supply shocks related to weather events and crop diseases—such as frost and drought affecting Arabica coffee growing regions and citrus greening and hurricanes impacting orange juice production. These are thin markets for soft commodities, where relatively small supply disruptions can lead to sharp global price changes rather than broad-based inflationary trends.
notes.why: The headline increase in this breakfast basket is primarily caused by a small group of weather-exposed crops with volatile supply conditions. Given the nature of these agricultural risks, input prices can remain elevated or volatile for extended periods. This underscores the sensitivity of soft commodity prices to environmental factors rather than broader economic inflation.
